p3.title: Out-of-order partial delivery is moved in the ledger at the later leaf start, so asOf reads disagree and returns dated in the gap are rejected
p3.failure_scenario:
1. Dispatch [0,30) at T1. Delivery A [0,20) occurs at T3 and is confirmed first. Delivery B [20,30) occurs at T2 and is confirmed later.
2. B's customer-place segment gets validFrom T3, while the Delivery row says occurredAt T2.
3. For asOf in [T2,T3), getDeliveries shows B but getInventory still shows the 10 in transit.
4. A return of B's goods with occurredAt in [T2,T3) reaches ReturnStockPrimitives.receive, then replaceRange, then leaf(c,seg,at). That throws REJECTED REVISION_CONFLICT on every retry, the same permanent-rejection pattern s4-sales-07 removed for deliveries.
p3.evidence: FulfillmentStockPrimitives.java:53 sets `Instant transferAt=instant(selected.get("validFrom")).isAfter(at)?instant(selected.get("validFrom")):at` and uses it for transferRangeReleasingCustody, while DeliveryTransfers and Deliveries keep occurredAt=at. The s4h-sales README discloses the ledger timing.
p3.fix: Record the transfer from the ancestor leaf that was valid at `at` with true valid-time history, or give later consumers of that segment a reconciliation path for gap-dated facts.

p3.title: [residual s4-sales-04] Item-scope sale eligibility excludes outside-warehouse stock by a place-kind denylist over free-text Places.kind
p3.failure_scenario: A deployment models customer sites as Places.kind 'EXTERNAL_CUSTOMER', the vocabulary of the Step 2 V6/V7 fixtures, or any other non-listed kind. SalesCommands accepts any existing place as destinationId. After delivering 20, getObject or getWork at item scope again report the delivered 20 as eligible and unreserved, which is the s4-sales-04 defect. Write paths still reject it (requireWarehouse), so read and write disagree.
p3.evidence: QualityEligibility.java:63 is `OUTSIDE_WAREHOUSE=Set.of("TRANSIT","CUSTOMER","SUPPLIER")`, and :71 skips only those kinds. SalesCommands.java:17 only checks that the destination place exists. No place-kind enumeration exists in the CDS, the migrations or contracts/domain-vocabulary.json. The verifier recommended excluding non-INTERNAL_STORAGE places or requiring internal custody.
p3.fix: Assess SELL eligibility only for INTERNAL_STORAGE segments with an internal custodian, the same predicate requireWarehouse uses, or enforce a closed Places.kind vocabulary.

p3.title: The dispatch continuous-authority check collects boundaries from every Restriction and DispositionBasis in the organization and rejects when there are more than 500
p3.failure_scenario: In a busy organization, a truthful dispatch backdated by a day (occurredAt at or after the pick) collects every Restriction and DispositionBasis validFrom, validUntil and releasedAt boundary in (at, now], for any segment, controlScope or item. Past 500 instants the command returns REJECTED INSUFFICIENT_ELIGIBLE_QUANTITY 'too fragmented' even though the allocation's own authority was continuous. prepare also runs twice per command, each time doing two full assess calls per instant.
p3.evidence: FulfillmentCommands.java:55-58 loops `for(var row:r.rows(c,table))` over all Restrictions and DispositionBases without filtering by controlScope or segment, and has `if(checked.size()>500)throw new DomainError("REJECTED",...)`.
p3.fix: Restrict candidate boundaries to rows whose controlScope or segment projects onto the allocation range, and to the item's lot, regulatory decisions and policy.

p3.title: Recall re-scope keeps the v1 RECALL_EXCLUDED_SCOPE duty OPEN over a range that is now inside the current scope
p3.failure_scenario:
1. Investigation [0,60). v1 scope is [0,25), which opens an excluded-scope duty for [25,60).
2. An ADMIN re-scopes v2 to [0,50) and records an EXCEPTION over [25,50), which carries its own residual duty.
3. The v1 excluded-scope review for [25,60) stays OPEN, so [25,50) has both an 'excluded' review and an in-scope exception residual. The stale duty can only be waived by an ADMIN.
p3.evidence: openExcluded (RecallCommands.java:70) only prevents opening another excluded duty. Nothing narrows or retires the earlier version's excluded duty when a later version includes its range. rescopeAfterRecoveryCarriesPhysicalFactsAndClosesTruthfully asserts this state.
p3.fix: On re-scope, mark the part of an open earlier excluded-scope duty that the new version covers as superseded or invalid, through an audited duty re-scope.

verified.title: Delivery timeliness is judged against the order revision current at confirmation, so a revision recorded after the delivery occurred rewrites past compliance
verified.failure_scenario:
1. Order line v1 is 100 with dueAt T+100. Dispatch 30 at T; the allocation is CONSUMED.
2. The carrier delivers at T+50, on time. The provisional observation is recorded at T+55.
3. At T+60 the customer pulls the order's due date for the remaining 70 to T+40. reviseSalesOrder is APPLIED: no allocation is EXECUTABLE or SUSPENDED, and dueAt is not a preserved term.
4. At T+70 the proof of delivery is verified and recordDelivery runs. sales.currentLine returns v2, and occurredAt T+50 is after v2's dueAt T+40, so legitimate=0 and legitimateRanges=[].
5. Result: Work goal and invoice contribution are 0, and a DELIVERY_RESTRICTION_RESPONSE for 30 is opened. That duty kind has no resolve or waive path (ObligationClosureCatalog.java:48), so it blocks closeWork permanently.
6. Confirming the same delivery at T+58, before the revision, would have recognized all 30. The outcome depends on confirmation order.
Mirror case: a late delivery at T+120 is followed by a retroactive extension to T+200 before confirmation. It is credited in full and the past violation disappears, although plan line 202 says a due-date change keeps 원 약속·현재 약속·과거 위반.
verified.evidence: DeliveryCommands.java:26 calls `var line=sales.currentLine(c,row.get("salesLineId").toString())` and zeroes legitimate when occurredAt is after line.dueAt. SalesCommands.java:30 currentLine resolves the revision current at the caller's knownAt, not the revision in force at the delivery's occurredAt. SalesRows gives revisions effectiveAt equal to their recording time, so the in-force revision is derivable but unused. In the new test deliveryInsideAnAgreedDueDateExtensionCountsAndADeliveryAfterAShortenedDueDateDoesNot, both revisions are recorded before the delivery occurs, so this path is untested.
verified.fix: Judge the delivery against the order line in force at the delivery occurredAt: the latest revision with effectiveAt at or before occurredAt in the previousLineId chain. Record the current promise separately for history. Add a test where the revision is recorded after the occurrence but before confirmation, in both directions.

verdict.reasoning: The scenario is reachable, so I could not refute it. DeliveryCommands.java:26 calls sales.currentLine. SalesCommands.java:30 resolves the revision through the mutable Orders.currentRevision pointer at confirmation time, not the revision in force at the delivery's occurredAt. reviseSalesOrder (SalesCommands.java:23) is blocked only by EXECUTABLE/SUSPENDED allocations or by changes to preserved terms. dueAt is not a preserved term, and valid() (line 18) has no future-date check. So a revision recorded between occurrence and confirmation decides whether legitimate is 30 or 0. Confirming before the revision gives a different, permanent result, because Delivery rows are never re-judged. The new test (FulfillmentPostgresTest:328) records both revisions before each delivery, so this order dependence is untested. It also contradicts D12 ('기한변경 후 위반 유지') and plan :144/:202. I downgrade to P3 for three reasons. (a) The harmful direction requires a sales user to enter a dueAt that is already in the past when the revision is recorded (T+40 entered at T+60). That is an unusual input, and the system is then applying the contract exactly as stated. (b) In the lenient direction, the past violation survives where the Work goal carries a dueAt: AssessmentService.java:37/92 recomputes the goal as of the GoalVersion dueAt using deliveries whose occurredAt is at or before that time, and deadlineViolated is sticky. (c) The trigger window is only the gap between POD occurrence and verification. The unclosable DELIVERY_RESTRICTION_RESPONSE is the existing fail-closed catalog design (ObligationClosureCatalog.java:48), not new behaviour. The fix direction (in-force-at-occurredAt revision via previousLineId/effectiveAt) is correct and cheap.

verified.title: A second return report is closed as a duplicate against another observation's canonical receipt without verifying its own event, time or evidence
verified.failure_scenario:
1. Delivery of 30. Authorization A1 covers [0,10). Observation O1 (event E1) is confirmed with canonical C1, creating Receipt R1 for [0,10).
2. The customer later ships 10 more boxes. Ops issue authorization A2. authorizeReturn does not subtract ranges already received, so A2 can again cover [0,10).
3. An agent with only the receiveReturn RECORD capability records observation O2: a different eventId E2, occurredAt two weeks later, and the default range [0,10).
4. The agent confirms receiveReturn{returnId:O2, canonicalOccurrenceId:C1}. existing=R1 overlaps. same() compares only range, delivery, customer, item, lot, unit and place, not occurredAt or event. The canonical equals R1's.
5. requireCanonical verifies C1 against O1, not O2. r.confirmed(O2) runs, then reconcileDuplicateReturnObservation marks O2's RETURN_RECONCILIATION RESOLVED with basis VERIFIED_TRADE_OBSERVATION and evidence C1.
6. Result: E2 was never matched or verified, the goods that physically arrived are in no ledger, and no duty remains.
verified.evidence: TradeObservationRemedy.java:19-29 checks only CONFIRMED state, subject keys and range, then calls service.applyTradeObservation with the prior receipt's canonical. Unlike apply(), it has no occurredAt equality check and no evidence binding O2's event to C1. ResponsibilityService.java:106 sets status RESOLVED with basis VERIFIED_TRADE_OBSERVATION. ReturnCommands.java:38-40 is the duplicate branch: it verifies the canonical against prior.observationId, then confirms the new observation. ObligationClosureCatalog.java:45 defines RETURN_RECONCILIATION closure as 'verified receiveReturn confirmation of the same observation'. Plan §6 line 208 keeps reconciliation responsibility when event linkage is unconfirmed. Test otherReportsOfReceivedReturnCloseAgainstTheOneReceipt confirms the second report with the first report's canonical.
verified.fix: Close a duplicate report only when its own event or claim has been reconciled to the same canonical through matchSourceIdentity/linkCanonicalOccurrence, and require an equal occurredAt. Otherwise keep the duty open, or close it with a typed human reconciliation or waiver decision.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed. In the duplicate branch (ReturnCommands.java:40), the canonical is verified only against the prior receipt's observation (prior.observationId). TradeObservationRemedy.reconcileDuplicateReturnObservation (lines 19-29) checks CONFIRMED state, subject keys and an exact range, then resolves the RETURN_RECONCILIATION duty through service.applyTradeObservation (basis VERIFIED_TRADE_OBSERVATION, ResponsibilityService:109). Unlike apply() (line 35) and the self/new branches (ReturnCommands:38/41, which check eventId against fact.occurrenceIdentity), it never checks occurredAt and never checks that O2's eventId is a chain of the canonical. Intake also never validates that eventId exists as an evidence Event (prepare only calls uuid(s,"eventId")). authorizeReturn (line 25) checks only that the range is inside the delivery, not against ranges already received, so a second authorization over [0,10) is accepted. The worker's own test (ReturnGatewayPostgresTest:179, the 'late' report under a new authorization) codifies exactly this path. If the second arrival is real goods booked against an already-returned range, a holder of the RECORD capability closes the only duty by citing another observation's canonical, and the goods sit outside any ledger with no owner. This contradicts plan §6 :208 (an unconfirmed event link keeps the reconciliation responsibility). The infrastructure for a proper link exists (matchSourceIdentity/linkCanonicalOccurrence in EvidenceReconciliationCommands), and the s4h-recall README says no waiver path exists for wrong return observations, so this branch is being used as an unverified closure path. Mitigation: it needs a mis-scoped manager authorization plus an agent choosing C1 (citing its own C2 is HELD), so P2 rather than P1.

verified.title: [residual s4-settle-02] A post-match delivery or receipt correction leaves an UNSATISFIED settlement with no duty, and the new NOT_OPEN gate blocks every adjustment
verified.failure_scenario:
1. Sale line 100 at 1000 KRW. Delivery 100. The SALE invoice for 100 is matched as MATCHED, with no duty.
2. A verified correction sets the delivery to 98. correctionImpact opens only DELIVERY_CORRECTED_DEFICIT 2.
3. getSettlement now returns contributionState CHANGED, result UNSATISFIED, currentQuantityDifference 2.
4. A MANAGER waives the deficit duty ('customer accepts 98').
5. Result: no owner exists for the 2-unit / 2000 KRW overbilling, and nothing can act on it:
   - recordSettlementAdjustment returns REJECTED SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE_NOT_OPEN, because dutyRootId is null.
   - matchInvoice returns INVOICE_ALREADY_MATCHED.
   - The settlement stays UNSATISFIED permanently.
The same happens to a DIFFERENCE match whose duty was RESOLVED before the correction, and to a PURCHASE match whose receipt chain is superseded (UNVERIFIED, no settlement duty).
verified.evidence: SettlementState.java:40-45 re-derives the contribution at read and closure time only. DeliveryCorrection.correctionImpact (DeliveryCorrection.java:27-37) never touches Matches or opens SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE. SettlementCommands.java:65 rejects adjustments unless the match is DIFFERENCE and state.open(dutyRootId) holds. The s4h-settle README lists this hook as an unfulfilled request to the sales owner. The verdict's narrowed claim was that 'the difference can be left with no owner'.
verified.fix: When a delivery correction or receipt-chain change alters the recognized contribution of a reference that has Matches, open a SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty keyed to the correction for each such Match, in the same transaction, and let adjustments and resolution target that duty. Add a SALE PostgreSQL test: match, correct to 98, waive the deficit, then expect an open settlement duty.

verdict.reasoning: The scenario is reachable. DeliveryCorrection.correctionImpact (DeliveryCorrection.java:27-36) opens only DELIVERY_CORRECTED_DEFICIT and has no settlement hook (grep: SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE is created only at SettlementCommands:53/61). After a MANAGER waives the deficit, SettlementState.assess (lines 38-46) reports CHANGED/UNSATISFIED, and no OPEN duty owns the overbilling. Two parts of the claim are wrong, though. First, this is not a NEW defect: it is the residual of s4-settle-02, which the s4h-settle README declares open ('MATCHED 송장은 정정 뒤 owner 있는 정산 의무가 없다'). Second, the NOT_OPEN gate (SettlementCommands:65) is not causal. Even without it, an adjustment cannot make a CHANGED match SATISFIED (assess requires state CURRENT and the immutable qd==0), adjustments never create duties, and the gate is the correct fix for s4-settle-04/08. A CREDIT_NOTE related to the original opens a review duty (SettlementCommands:53), which gives a manual owner path, but that duty closes only by waiver and the original stays UNSATISFIED and ownerless afterwards. This is the same open P2 as claim 5; count it once.

p3.title: Backdated dispatch is rejected outright once the org has >500 authority boundaries after the occurrence time
p3.failure_scenario: requireContinuousAuthority adds validFrom/validUntil/releasedAt of every Restrictions and DispositionBases row in the organization (not only those touching the segment/item) that falls in (occurredAt, now]. In an organization with more than 500 such instants since the dispatch occurrence (a few days of QC activity on unrelated items), every dispatch with a past occurredAt is REJECTED/INSUFFICIENT_ELIGIBLE_QUANTITY 'history too fragmented' even though the allocation was continuously eligible.
p3.evidence: FulfillmentCommands.java:57-58: `for(String table:List.of("Restrictions","DispositionBases"))for(var row:r.rows(c,table)){add.accept(row.get("validFrom"));…}` with no segment/item/controlScope filter, and `if(checked.size()>500)throw new DomainError("REJECTED","INSUFFICIENT_ELIGIBLE_QUANTITY",…)`.
p3.fix: Filter boundary rows to those that can project onto the segment (same controlScope/item/genealogy ancestors) before collecting instants, or rely solely on QualityEligibility.nextValidityBoundary iteration; keep the cap as a last resort.

p3.title: Out-of-order partial delivery reintroduces the asOf disagreement between Delivery and inventory for that case
p3.failure_scenario: Dispatch 30 at T1; delivery A [0,20) occurred T3 confirmed first; delivery B [20,30) occurred T2<T3 confirmed later. Delivery/DeliveryTransfer rows carry T2 but the customer-place segment gets validFrom=T3 (transferAt = leaf validFrom). getDeliveries asOf in [T2,T3) returns B as delivered while getInventory at the same asOf shows [20,30) still in transit (the s4-sales-09/12 disagreement, now limited to this path).
p3.evidence: FulfillmentStockPrimitives.java:51: `Instant transferAt=instant(selected.get("validFrom")).isAfter(at)?instant(selected.get("validFrom")):at;` while :52 inserts DeliveryTransfers with occurredAt=at. Worker README s4-sales-07 declares this limitation.
p3.fix: Record the genealogy child with validFrom=at and let replaceRange accept a child earlier than the current leaf when the leaf was itself created by a later-dated sibling delivery, or surface an explicit unknown ('LEDGER_DATED_AT_LEAF_START') on inventory reads for that range.

p3.title: RECOVERED prerequisites and conflicts for recall processing span all investigations on the same root segment
p3.failure_scenario: Two investigations A and B on the same root segment: A records RECOVERED [0,25). Under B (its own ADMIN approval), DISPOSED [0,25) is accepted because recoveredOnRoot is computed from all Actions on the root regardless of investigationId, and B's own RECOVERED [0,25) is refused with RECALL_RANGE_ALREADY_RECOVERED. B's closure partition then counts a DISPOSED whose recovery fact belongs to A.
p3.evidence: RecallCommands.java:123 `var recoveredOnRoot=existing.stream().filter(x->"RECOVERED".equals(x.get("kind"))&&root.equals(x.get("rootSegmentId"))).toList();` and :147 `var recovered=recoveredOnRoot…` used for the DISPOSED prerequisite; `facts` (per investigation) is used only for the terminal partition.
p3.fix: Use investigation-scoped RECOVERED facts for the DISPOSED prerequisite, and make the root-wide check a distinct CONFLICT that names the other investigation.

p3.title: CONSUMED_LOST/EXCEPTION over stock that never left the warehouse is still accepted while the ledger holds it
p3.failure_scenario: Investigation opened on a warehouse segment (no dispatch). An actor records CONSUMED_LOST [0,25) with a verified RECALL_CONSUMED_LOST canonical. recoveredOverlap is empty (no RECOVERED action), so the heldQuantity guard never runs; the closure partition reports 25 consumed/lost while QuantitySegments still hold those 25 units under the recall restriction.
p3.evidence: RecallCommands.java:126: `if(Set.of("CONSUMED_LOST","EXCEPTION").contains(kind))for(var held:recoveredOverlap)if(stock.heldQuantity(…)>0)throw …` — the held-stock check is only applied to ranges that have a RECOVERED action.
p3.fix: Apply heldQuantity(root, start, q) to the whole CONSUMED_LOST/EXCEPTION range, not only to the RECOVERED overlap.

p3.title: Duplicate return observation is closed by citing another observation's canonical without verifying its own evidence
p3.failure_scenario: O1 confirmed as Receipt R1 for [0,10). A second provisional observation O2 (new eventId, same range) is recorded. The RECORD actor confirms O2 passing R1's canonicalOccurrenceId: requireCanonical is run against O1's scope, O2 is marked CONFIRMED and its RETURN_RECONCILIATION duty resolves, although no verified source was ever linked to O2. Any same-range provisional report can thus be closed by reference alone; O2 is CONFIRMED with no Receipt and ReturnQueries still reports it PROVISIONAL (worker-declared).
p3.evidence: ReturnCommands.java:280: `evidence.requireCanonical(c,canonical,"RETURN_RECEIPT",prior.get("itemId")…,prior.get("observationId")…);r.confirmed(c,t.get("ID")…);remedy.reconcileDuplicateReturnObservation(…)` — physicalScopeId checked is prior.observationId, not t.ID.
p3.fix: Require a verified chain whose physical scope is O2 (or an explicit DUPLICATE_REPORT reconciliation decision) before closing O2's duty, and project O2 as DUPLICATE_OF R1 in ReturnQueries.

p3.title: ManagementCoverage accepts authority that fully covers any single dimension, regardless of the others
p3.failure_scenario: authorizeReturn/decideReturnDisposition/approveRecall/disposeQuantity with scopes {ITEM:[P], PLACE:[C,W], WORK:[w]}: a manager whose only ManagementAuthority row is ITEM=P passes coverage even though no PLACE value is covered, because covers() returns true when the values of any one dimension are all matched.
p3.fix: Document that a ManagementAuthority row is dimension-wide authority (ITEM-wide covers all places) or, if per-value authority on every dimension is intended by plan §7.1, require coverage of every dimension present in the scope map.
